home.title: Report a cyber crime
home.lede: This portal takes complaints of cyber crime, with special focus on crimes against women and children. Choose a path. The same acknowledgement is shown before every filing.
home.helplineKicker: In an emergency call 112. Women helpline 181. Cyber crime helpline
home.cardWcBody: Sexual cyber crimes against women or children. You may file in your name, or report anonymously. Anonymous reports receive confirmation and cannot be tracked.
home.cardFinBody: UPI, wallet, net-banking, card, investment. A named complaint can be tracked. Call 1930 as well — the hold clock starts from the first report.
home.cardOtherBody: Hacking, impersonation, phishing, harassment and other cyber offences that are not sexual crimes against women or children and not financial fraud.
home.ticker1: Through Report & Check Suspect, citizens can report website URLs, WhatsApp and Telegram handles, phone numbers, email IDs, SMS headers, and social-media URLs.
home.ticker2: Important: messages impersonating officials of the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) are circulating. Do not share OTPs or remote-access apps.
home.ticker3: Financial fraud: call 1930 first, then complete the full complaint on this portal. The 24-hour full-complaint rule is printed on the acknowledgement.
home.learnManualBody: How this portal takes a complaint, what an acknowledgement number is, and how tracking works.
home.learnSafetyBody: Practical steps to reduce UPI, OTP and impersonation fraud.
home.learnAwarenessBody: What lurks in cyberspace, and how employees and families can act.
home.learnDigestBody: A short briefing from I4C on current fraud modus operandi.

ack.title: Acknowledgement
ack.kicker: Read before you file — the same notice on every track
ack.p1: This portal is an initiative of Government of India to facilitate victims/complainants to report cyber crime complaints online. This portal caters to complaints pertaining to cyber crimes only with special focus on cyber crimes against women and children. Complaints reported on this portal are dealt by law enforcement agencies/ police based on the information available in the complaints. It is imperative to provide correct and accurate details while filing complaint for prompt action.
ack.p2: Please contact local police in case of an emergency or for reporting crimes other than cyber crimes. National police helpline number is 112. National women helpline number is 181 and Cyber Crime Helpline is 1930.
ack.check: I have read and understood the information provided above.

login.title: Citizen login

login.name: Full name
login.otpSent: OTP sent to the number you entered. Enter the code from the mock SMS.
login.otpWrong: That code does not match the mock SMS. Enter the six digits shown in the toast.

checklist.title: Check list for complainant
checklist.intro: Please keep this information ready before filing your complaint:
checklist.m2: Incident details (minimum 200 characters) without any special characters (#$@*^"~!]).
checklist.m3: Soft copy of any national Id ( Voter Id, Driving license, Passport, PAN Card, Aadhaar Card) of complainant in .jpeg, .jpg, .png format (file size should not more than 5 MB).
checklist.m4: In case of financial fraud, please keep following information ready:
checklist.m5: Soft copy of all the relevant evidences related to the cyber crime (not more than 10 MB each)
checklist.o1: Suspected website URLs/ Social Media handles (wherever applicable)
checklist.o2v: Soft copy of photograph of suspect in .jpeg, .jpg, .png format (not more than 5 MB)
checklist.o2vi: Any other document through which suspect can be identified.
checklist.deadline: The 24-hour full-complaint rule: complete this form within 24 hours of the first report so every legal right stays open. Cited: helpline SOP / printed acknowledgement.
checklist.continue: I have this information — start the form

suspect.title: Report & Check Suspect
suspect.lede: This mock has one honest screen. On the live portal this is where a citizen submits a suspect identifier — a URL, handle, number, email, or SMS header — without filing a full complaint.
suspect.body: No lookup runs here. Nothing is sent to a watch-list. If you have a full incident to report, use Register a Complaint on the Home page. If you already have an acknowledgement number, use Track your Complaint.

learn.title: Learning Corner
learn.lede: Four short notes. Each is one screen deep.
learn.manualBody: A complaint on this portal is not an FIR. Filing issues a 14-digit acknowledgement number (date of filing plus a serial). Trackable complaints are those filed after citizen login. Anonymous reports, available only for sexual cyber crimes against women and children, receive a confirmation reference and cannot be tracked. Financial fraud should also be called in to 1930 — the first report starts the hold clock. Complete the full form within 24 hours of that first report.
learn.safetyBody: Do not share OTPs, PINs, or screen-sharing apps with anyone who calls as a bank or as I4C. Verify UPI names before you pay. A prize, job, or KYC message that asks you to install an app or read back an OTP is fraud. If money has already left, call 1930, tell your bank, and file on this portal. Keep the debit SMS — it is the fastest way to capture amount and time.
learn.awarenessBody: Most financial cyber crime against Indian citizens now travels over UPI and fake investment pages. Sexual image abuse against women and children has a dedicated anonymous path because the portal's own mandate is special focus on those crimes. Neither path is a substitute for 112 in an emergency.
learn.digestBody: Mock digest for 27 Aug 2026: mule accounts receiving UPI credits after “KYC update” messages; deepfake video calls impersonating relatives; emails using CEO I4C as sender display. None of these are requests from this portal. This digest does not update — one honest screen, then stop.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.lede: A short, honest page. This is not the live portal's full FAQ.
faq.a1: Cyber crimes only: sexual crimes against women and children, financial fraud, and other cyber crime. For any other crime, or an emergency, call 112.
faq.a2: Only for sexual cyber crimes against women and children, from the Women/Children card. Anonymous reports receive confirmation but cannot be tracked.
faq.q3: How do I track a complaint?
faq.a3: Track your Complaint, with the 14-digit acknowledgement number and the mobile you registered. A mock OTP will appear on screen. Unknown numbers return “no record found”. Anonymous references return the anonymous-boundary message.
faq.q4: Is a portal complaint an FIR?
faq.a4: No. The acknowledgement is a complaint record. An FIR is a separate police step.
faq.a5: No. This is a design prototype on mock data, frozen at 27 Aug 2026, 9:48 AM IST.

stubs.contactBody: On the live portal this page lists State/UT nodal officers and grievance officers. This mock does not publish those contacts. For a cyber financial emergency call 1930. For any emergency call 112. Women helpline 181.
stubs.feedbackBody: Feedback is not collected in this prototype. Nothing you type here is stored or sent.
stubs.policiesBody: This prototype is not a government website and has no hosting, archival, or linking policy of its own. Content is mock exploration under a Case Spine design contract.
stubs.privacyBody: No personal data leaves this browser. Name, mobile, OTP and complaint text sit in session storage on this machine so the mock can be refreshed. Clear the site data to erase them.
stubs.disclaimerBody: Asha K., Saral Bank, Dhanvir Co-op Bank, PayMate Wallet, kubertraders@dvb, Sector-21 Cyber PS, and every acknowledgement number here are invented. Amounts and clocks are fixtures. This is not legal advice and not a live filing channel.
stubs.a11yBody: Pages use landmarks, labelled fields, skip-to-content, and visible focus. Text can be resized with A− / A / A+. Colour is never the only money-state signal — chips carry codes. This is a prototype, not a WCAG conformance claim.
